label: Ghee
comment: Desi ghee is boiled from butter churned from dahi.

about.text: Ghee is a type of clarified butter, originating in the Indian Subcontinent. It is a widely used butter for cooking especially in Indian cuisines and in Hindu religious rituals. Typically made from cow butter or buffalo butter, ghee is favoured for its nutty flavour and high smoke point allowing it to be heated at high temperatures without burning.

facts.v: Boil raw milk, cool to 43 °C, leave covered about 12 h, add a little dahi overnight, churn with water, simmer the butter into ghee; the desi route sets whole milk as dahi at room temperature, churns it to white butter and boils that in an open pan
Makhan heated to 110-120 °C with constant stirring until moisture is below 1 % and the curd particles brown; about 90 % of Indian ghee is made from makhan (c. 650,000 t a year)
Cream (high-fat 60-75 % is better than 40 %) heated straight to ghee at about 110-120 °C (120-140 °C in south India); takes longer and leaves more ghee residue, and washing the cream cuts residue
Melted butter held at about 80 °C for hours, the lowest serum layer (about 74 % of the water) drained, then heated to 110-120 °C
Moisture at most 0.3 % in one source, at most 3 % in another
At 100 °C or below milder; at about 120 °C strong, nutty, caramelised
Cow ghee deep yellow, buffalo ghee white with a yellowish-green tinge
about 80-85 % traditional, 88-92 % creamery butter, up to 90-95 % with indirect cream (one review)
